author: Forbes
description:
Anthropic filed for its blockbuster IPO on Monday, bringing the AI behemoth closer to what could be the largest public debuts in stock market history. The 335-page filing revealed the Claude maker generated around $16.3 billion in revenue for the first half of the year, up from $1.2 billion a year earlier, but incurred a $80.7 billion net loss for the first half of the year (most of which is due to a non-cash accounting charge). The company touts more than 300,000 enterprise customers, 250 of which spend over $10 million on Anthropic’s products every year. It plans to list under the ticker symbol “ANT” and is on track to go public as soon as mid-November.

Forbes estimates that its two most prominent cofounders: CEO Dario Amodei and his sister, Anthropic president Daniela Amodei, are worth $13.6 billion and $13.7 billion, respectively. Each cofounder owns an estimated 1.4% stake.

Read the full story on Forbes: https://www.forbes.com/sites/the-prompt/2026/10/27/inside-anthropics-ipo-p
title: Two Big AI Risks Revealed In Anthropic's New S-1 Filing

author: Forbes
description:
Robin Arzón has a superpower: saying exactly what we need to hear, exactly when we need to hear it.

If you haven't had the privilege of being a Robin mentee, allow us to introduce you. The VP and Head Instructor at Peloton (and mom, 27-time marathon runner AND podcast host, among other things) has built a devoted community by making people feel capable of taking on just about anything.

And if you ask the multi-hyphenate (a word we don't like to throw around for just anybody) how she manages it all, she'll be the first to tell you: "I kind of believe the concept of balance is bullsh*t."

On this week's episode of Forbes Talks Shop, Robin shares how she—instead of chasing balance—approaches living in alignment with her values and builds support systems that set her up for success.

Trust us, you'll want a notepad for this one. Watch the full conversation on our YouTube channel.

#RobinArzon #Peloton #ForbesTalksShop
title: Robin Arzon Talks Shop

author: Forbes
description:
Rain is developing AI-powered technology that equips existing aircraft with autonomous firefighting capabilities, helping firefighters respond to wildfires faster and potentially stop them before they spread.

In this episode of Forbes The Future Of, Rain cofounder and CEO Maxwell Brodie shares how surviving a devastating wildfire as a child inspired him to rethink wildfire response. He explains how Rain's technology works, why the first minutes of a wildfire are so critical and how autonomous aircraft could help firefighters combat increasingly destructive fires.
